note: Roast names are matched as strings only inside FromStr at the input boundary; all logic after parsing works on the Roast enum and unknown input is reported.
Signal.light is a String holding a closed red/green/yellow set, advanced by matching string literals with a catch-all arm and compared to "green"; an enum would let the compiler check the cases.
Member.role is a magic u8 (0-3) matched on literal numbers with a fallback arm and compared with == 2 / == 3; a closed set of roles that should be an enum.
Author names, message bodies and @mentions are genuinely free-form text used as map keys; no closed set of states is encoded in strings.
Request.method is a String compared against "GET"/"PUT"/"DELETE" literals in an if-else chain with a catch-all 405, so a typo or lowercase method silently falls through instead of being an enum.
Stack-machine tokens are parsed once at the boundary into the Op enum with a typed ParseError; execution matches exhaustively on Op, numbers are real data.
Order.payment_method and Order.shipping are magic u8 codes matched on literals (1/2/3 with _ fallbacks, shipping == 2 / == 1), a closed set that should be enums.
Job kind and priority strings are parsed via FromStr into Kind and Priority enums at the spec boundary with typed errors; job names and payloads are free-form data.

Event.kind ("restock"/"sale"/"damage"/"audit") and Item.category ("perishable"/"fragile"/...) are closed sets stored as strings and matched on literals with fallbacks, so the typo "retrun" is only caught at runtime.
Metric kind is parsed once into the MetricKind enum at the line boundary; metric names and label keys/values are an open-ended user-defined set, so strings are appropriate.
